cards.text: Elisha, the prophet known as the man of God, once brought a woman's son back to life (2 Kings 4:32-37). Now he has a word for her from the LORD. Something is coming to the land, and she needs to hear it.

cards.question: Elisha warns the woman that the LORD has decreed a seven-year ___ will come to the land.
With seven hard years coming, what does Elisha tell the woman and her household to do?

answers.text: Leave and live as foreigners wherever they can
Stay home and store up all the grain they can
Move inside the walls of Samaria and wait it out

cards.text: And she does it. No arguing, no 'let me sleep on it.' She takes her whole household and goes. Me? It took an ANGEL in the middle of the night to get me out of one junk drawer.

cards.question: The woman and her household live through the famine years in the land of the Philistines.

cards.text: Seven years go by, just like the LORD said. Then the woman brings her household back home from the land of the Philistines.

cards.question: Back home, the woman goes straight to the ___ to make an appeal.
After seven years away, what does the woman ask the king for?

answers.text: A new home in the city

cards.text: Meanwhile, the king is talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God. And the king wants the HIGHLIGHT REEL.

cards.question: What does the king ask Gehazi, Elisha's servant, to tell him?

answers.text: All the great things Elisha has done
Where Elisha has been staying lately
Why the famine lasted so many years

cards.question: Out of all of Elisha's great things, which one is Gehazi telling the king about?

answers.text: How Elisha brought the dead back to life
How Elisha split the waters of the Jordan
How Elisha made an iron axhead float

cards.question: Gehazi is right in the middle of that story when the woman comes in to appeal to the king.

cards.text: Friend, that TIMING. That's like telling your coworkers about the guy who saved your life, and he walks into the break room right as you say his name.

cards.question: Gehazi tells the king this is the woman. Who else does Gehazi point out?
When the king asks the woman about it, she tells him Gehazi got the story mixed up.

cards.text: She confirms it. Now the king has heard it from the servant AND from the woman herself. Time for the king to do something.

cards.question: So the king appoints an ___ for the woman.
What does the king tell the officer to do for the woman?

answers.text: Give back all that was hers plus all the field produced
Give back her house but keep her field for the crown
Give her a different field close to the king's palace

cards.text: Not just the house. Not just the land. Everything that field produced from the day she left until now. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and all I came out with was dust in my mustache.

findings.problem: The question types repeat the same pattern three times: a fill in the blank followed right away by a multiple choice (cards 2-3, 7-8, 17-18). Multiple choice also dominates the stop, with 6 cards against 3 fill in the blank and 3 true or false.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The story card runs four to five sentences: "And she does it." / "No arguing, no 'let me sleep on it.'" / "She takes her whole household and goes." / "Me?" / "It took an ANGEL..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the woman's. She obeys promptly when told to leave. Papa Dorin's comparison, needing an angel to get out of the drawer, implies he was slow or reluctant to leave. In his backstory he couldn't leave the drawer on his own, and he said yes after asking for one minute. The comparison isn't the same action, and it misstates his story.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Goes straight to the ___" adds immediacy. 2 Kings 8:3 says only that when she returned, she went to the king. It gives no timing.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "The king wants the HIGHLIGHT REEL" gives away the answer to card 10 ("All the great things Elisha has done"). It also rules out both wrong answers before the baker picks.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card is only a reaction joke. It tells no part of 2 Kings 8:5 that wasn't already told on cards 11-12, so it doesn't move the passage along.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The comparison has the wrong person walking in. In the comparison, the guy who saved your life (the Elisha role) walks into the break room. In 2 Kings 8:5, the one who walks in is the woman whose son was raised, the person who was helped, while Gehazi tells about Elisha. The actions don't match.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card is three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The article "an" before the blank rules out the wrong answer "priest" ("an priest"). Only "officer" and "elder" fit grammatically.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card is four sentences: "Not just the house." / "Not just the land." / "Everything that field produced..." / "Friend, I spent YEARS..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "All I came out with was dust in my mustache" contradicts his backstory. When he left the drawer, he was renewed: sharp edges, a clean apron, a mustache fuller than ever, and the whole Dorinverse. The joke changes his own story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
